content: If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on how to safely discard the medication. This medication is used either alone or in combination with other medications to prevent a serious bacterial infection known as Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC). Rifabutin belongs to a class of drugs called rifamycin antibiotics. It works by stopping the growth of bacteria. This antibiotic is effective only against bacterial infections and will not treat viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. If stomach upset occurs, take it with food. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, weight, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve before completing the course. Common side effects of this medication may include diarrhea, stomach upset, changes in taste, nausea, or vomiting. Additionally, it may cause your urine, sweat, saliva, or tears to turn a brown-orange color. This discoloration is harmless and will resolve once the medication is discontinued. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, or cramping. A serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, seek medical help immediately if you notice symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking rifabutin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other rifamycin antibiotics (such as rifampin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Rifabutin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine). Inform your healthcare provider if you are scheduled to receive any vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. If you have HIV, be aware that breast milk can transmit the virus to your baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Rifabutin can accelerate the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver function tests and complete blood counts) should be performed regularly to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Be sure to keep all medical and lab appointments. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
